mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the 60-day forward window, indicating a growth slowdown that negates the positive earnings signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, exceeding a 2% month-over-month decline, signals a supply shock that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies struggle with input disruptions and rising costs.
failure_condition: SPX posts positive 20-day returns in > 55% of instances following a 2%+ INDPRO drop, indicating markets are shrugging off the supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate, with the 3-month change exceeding 0.5 percentage points, signals a weakening labor market that will pressure consumer spending and weigh on S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Retail sales (RSAFS) show positive YoY growth in the 60-day forward window, contradicting the negative consumer spending signal from rising unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that will slow economic growth and produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX posts positive 20-day returns in > 45% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, indicating markets are not responding negatively to the restrictive policy.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% year-over-year and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is rising, it signals a weakening consumer sector that will weigh on S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 10% YoY AND UNRATE rising
failure_condition: Consumer discretionary sector outperforms the broader market over the 60-day forward window, indicating consumer health is not deteriorating as the signal suggests.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is above its 12-month moving average and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 3%, it signals a favorable supply-demand balance that will support positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX posts negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances when INDPRO > 12m MA and FEDFUNDS < 3%, indicating the favorable supply-demand conditions are not boosting equity prices.

mechanism_narrative: A flattening yield curve, with the 10-year Treasury yield (DGS10) falling below the 2-year yield (DGS2), signals a growth slowdown that will produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The yield curve steepens (DGS10 - DGS2 > 0.5%) during the 60-day forward window, contradicting the growth slowdown signal from the initial inversion.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) is growing by more than 200,000 jobs per month, it signals a tight labor market that will boost wage growth and support consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% AND PAYEMS growth > 200k per month
failure_condition: Real average hourly earnings (AHETPI) decline over the 20-day forward window, indicating that the tight labor market is not translating into wage growth as expected.
